statements.text: Pseudonymisation lowers risk but the data is generally still regarded as personal data in many jurisdictions, because re-identification remains possible with additional information; exactly where the line sits depends on jurisdiction and legal advice.
statements.quote: Recital 26 (EUR-Lex, opened): "should be considered to be information on an identifiable natural person"; identifiability turns on "all the means reasonably likely to be used" and "all objective factors" such as "the costs of and the amount of time required for identification"; "The principles of data protection should therefore not apply to anonymous information". ICO (opened): "Yes. Pseudonymised data is personal data in the hands of someone who holds the additional information." Recital 28 (EUR-Lex): "The application of pseudonymisation to personal data can reduce the risks to the data subjects concerned".
